attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Dermatology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Complaints of itchy skin over the past several months

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 21-year-old male with seasonal allergic rhinitis and atopic dermatitis who returns for follow-up, previously evaluated in January 2020 for recurrent rash. He reports that the symptoms are worse during the winter and after hot showers. He has been using over-the-counter creams with partial relief but notes that the rash tends to recur in the same locations. He denies recent travel, new medications, or contact with sick individuals.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Atopic dermatitis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis

His past medical history is significant for seasonal allergies during the spring.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Wisdom teeth extraction (age 18)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Cetirizine 10 mg oral tablet daily as needed during allergy season
- Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 2 sprays in each nostril once daily (spring months)

ALLERGIES:
Tree and grass pollens (seasonal), Dust mites, No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
Family history reveals that his mother has a history of asthma.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 drinks on weekends). Occupation: University student (junior, biology major).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, there are multiple erythematous patches with excoriations over the flexural surfaces of the elbows. An image of the rash is provided. No pustules, vesicles, or drainage are seen. The remainder of the skin and systemic examination is normal.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies, including complete blood count and metabolic panel, are unremarkable.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Dermatology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Rash that has been coming and going for several years

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He says it becomes worse during certain seasons and sometimes after bathing. He has tried different creams from the pharmacy with only mild benefit. He denies fever, weight loss, or recent medication use.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Wisdom teeth extraction (age 18)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Cetirizine 10 mg oral tablet daily as needed during allergy season
- Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 2 sprays in each nostril once daily (spring months)

ALLERGIES:
Tree and grass pollens (seasonal), Dust mites, No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Atopic dermatitis (childhood)
- Father: Allergic rhinitis and asthma
- Younger brother: Seasonal allergies

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 drinks on weekends). Occupation: University student (junior, biology major).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Examination shows multiple erythematous patches with evidence of scratching and mild thickening of the skin along the inner aspect of the elbows. An image is provided. There is no discharge or tenderness.

LABORATORY DATA:
Routine blood work is within normal limits.
